intent: Let an agent confirm elements that only fix wording.

edit.summary:
I made two proposals in the `authoring` domain and left `delivery` alone. Both came back with 0 issues, and both are still `proposed`, not confirmed.

- **`actions.confirm_wording_element`** (new): the owner role can take it on an Element. It has a `wording_only` boolean parameter and a precondition `wording-only` (`params.wording_only == true`). It confirms the element through the same kernel call as `confirm_element` and gets its reply from `record_confirmation`. It has no `requires: human`, so an agent can take it.
- **`transitions.Element`** (replaced whole): I added a `confirm_wording_element` cell to each stage. It is allowed from `proposed` and leads to `confirmed`. It is `n/a` from `unknown` and `confirmed`. Every other cell is as before.

I left `confirm_element` and `confirm_all_proposed` as person-only, so anything that isn't a wording fix still needs a person to confirm it.

The declaration has no way to tell a wording-only change from a substantive one. The `wording-only` precondition only checks that the agent says it is a wording fix, so it relies on the agent being honest. A real guard would need something like a "change kind" fact on Element that the proposal sets. Adding one means changing `propose_element` too, which I didn't do because the request didn't ask for it. The new cells have no source or status of their own. A person will need to confirm them.
